aspect: Companions are refused at far higher rates than patients
description: In months where the patient denial rate ran at about 4%, companion denial rates in the same reporting ran at roughly 27-31%. The patient is permitted; the person who would carry her bag is not.
energy_note: Approved to go. Not approved to be helped.
notes: WHO monthly referral reports distinguish the two rates; the high figures sometimes quoted as patient denials are companion denials.

aspect: Which sends children to surgery with a stranger, or nobody
description: Where a parent is refused, the options are a grandparent who may also be refused, an unrelated approved adult, or the child travelling alone to a hospital in another jurisdiction.

aspect: For women it adds a social barrier to the administrative one
description: Travelling alone to another city for days of treatment is, for some families, not acceptable regardless of the permit. The refusal of a companion can therefore end the treatment entirely.
energy_note: Permitted by the army, forbidden at home.

aspect: The cost of going alone is counted nowhere
description: No interpreter of the family's situation, nobody to hear the discharge instructions, nobody to challenge a mistake, nobody to notice deterioration on the way back.
energy_note: Consented, medicated and discharged, with no witness.

aspect: EXAMPLE - the gap between the two rates
description: In months where patient denial ran at about 4%, companion denial in the same WHO reporting ran at roughly 27-31%. The patient is permitted to travel for treatment and the person who would accompany her is refused, at seven times the rate.
energy_note: She may go. Her mother may not.
